body:
## Purpose

Review fixes for #1907, targeting its branch (`kd/try_spatially_varying_canopy_height`). Each item below is independent, so take what is useful. The two bugs (2 and 3) and the ClimaCoupler break (1) are the important ones; the rest are tests, docs, and typos.

## 1. This PR breaks ClimaCoupler, and the fix

ClimaCoupler's bucket path (`ext/ClimaCouplerClimaLandExt/climaland_bucket.jl` on ClimaCoupler `main`) computes the bucket turbulent fluxes itself:

```julia
h_sfc = CL.surface_height(model, Y, p)
...
bucket_dest .= CL.turbulent_fluxes_at_a_point.(
    momentum_fluxes, p.drivers.P, p.drivers.T, p.drivers.q, p.drivers.u, coupled_atmos.h,
    T_sfc, q_sfc, roughness_model, update_T_sfc, update_q_sfc, h_sfc, displ,
    update_∂T_sfc∂T, update_∂q_sfc∂T, gustiness, earth_param_set,
)
```

With #1907 (checked in Julia on the branch):

- `ClimaLand.surface_height` no longer exists, so the first line throws `UndefVarError`.
- `turbulent_fluxes_at_a_point` now takes `reference` before `earth_param_set`, so the 17-argument call throws `MethodError`.
- `CoupledAtmosphere{FT, T}(h, gustiness)`, which ClimaCoupler uses for both the bucket and the integrated land, now defaults to `ReferenceAboveApparentSink`. This is a behavior change, not an error.

ClimaCoupler's compat is `ClimaLand = "1.12.2"`, so it would pick up the next 1.x release and break at run time. The "downstream ClimaCoupler.jl" check on #1907 does not catch this. That job currently fails for every recent PR and on `main`. On #1907 it stops earlier, when GeoMakie fails to precompile (`UndefVarError: timed_ticklabelspace_reset not defined in Makie`).

**Fix in this PR (ClimaCoupler keeps working unchanged):**

- `surface_height` is a deprecated alias of `surface_elevation` (`Base.@deprecate`).
- The form of `turbulent_fluxes_at_a_point` without `reference` is a deprecated method. It measures `h_atmos` from the ground, as before #1907, so ClimaCoupler's bucket fluxes do not change. It has no `depwarn` because it runs inside broadcast kernels. It does not create method ambiguities: `Test.detect_ambiguities(ClimaLand; recursive = true)` is empty.
- Tests for both, plus a test of the `CoupledAtmosphere` default reference.

**Follow-up in ClimaCoupler**, when it bumps its ClimaLand compat:

```diff
-    h_sfc = CL.surface_height(model, Y, p)
+    z_sfc = CL.surface_elevation(model, Y, p)
 ...
         update_q_sfc,
-        h_sfc,
+        z_sfc,
         displ,
         update_∂T_sfc∂T,
         update_∂q_sfc∂T,
         gustiness,
+        coupled_atmos.reference,
         earth_param_set,
     )
```

**Behavior change for coupled runs (kept as is):** with the `CoupledAtmosphere` default, the coupled integrated land treats `atmos_h` as the height above the apparent sink for momentum, `d + z_0m` above the ground. So does the bucket's `q_sfc`, which ClimaLand computes from `atmos.reference`. I kept this default. It is the SurfaceFluxes convention for an atmosphere that does not resolve the canopy. With CLM canopy heights, the old convention fails wherever the lowest atmospheric level lies below `d + z_0m` (about 23 m for a 30 m forest): SurfaceFluxes returns NaN there. Until ClimaCoupler passes `coupled_atmos.reference`, its bucket flux call (the deprecated form) keeps the old convention. For the bucket the two differ only by `z_0m` = 1 cm.

## 2. Bug: soil and snow below a canopy used the forcing's reference

`subcanopy_forcing` returns heights above the ground with `reference = ReferenceAboveSurface()`. `LandModel` and `SoilCanopyModel` did not pass that `reference` to `Snow.update_surf_temp!` and `Soil.update_soil_surface_temperature!`. Those then default to the reference of the atmospheric forcing, which is `ReferenceAboveApparentSink` for ERA5 and CRU-JRA. In global runs, the ground solves therefore added their own `d + z_0m` on top of the sub-canopy height.

Example: a column with a 10 m canopy and apparent-sink forcing stored a soil `Δz_eff` of 7.543 m. The sub-canopy height is 7.533 m. The effect is small (soil `z_0m` is 1 cm, snow less), but the conventions were inconsistent.

- Fix: forward `reference` in the three ground solve calls.
- Tests:
  - a column `SoilCanopyModel` under apparent-sink forcing, which fails without the fix;
  - a soil and snow `Δz_eff` check in the inland-water `LandModel` test, which uses ERA5 forcing.

## 3. Bug: `compute_Δz_eff` arguments swapped in the snow solve

`Snow.solve_for_surface_temp_at_a_point` called `compute_Δz_eff(atmos_h, displ, z_0m, reference)`, but the signature is `(h_atmos, z_0m, displ, reference)`. This only affects the initial `q_sfc` guess of the snow solve, which is off by `z_0m` because snow has no displacement height. It is still a bug.

## 4. Two soil tests compared a copy with itself

In `test/standalone/Soil/climate_drivers.jl`, `turbulent_fluxes!(::EnergyHydrology)` was removed. After that, the two checks that the stored fluxes match a separate solve at the skin temperature compared a copy of the stored fluxes with itself. The frozen-soil one also ran the update on the unfrozen `Y, p`.

I restored both checks using an independent solve through the generic `ClimaLand.turbulent_fluxes!`. For the soil, it holds `T_sfc` at the stored skin temperature, as the removed method did, so no source code needed to come back.

## 5. Docs, typos, and small cleanups

- Docstrings that contradicted the code:
  - the `PrescribedAtmosphere` field docs said the default reference was the apparent sink, but the constructor default is `ReferenceAboveSurface`;
  - `CoupledAtmosphere` now documents its `reference` keyword and default;
  - `compute_ρ_sfc` evaluates the density at the displacement height, and `Δh` is the height above it (`Δz_eff`), not the height above the apparent sink.
- `subcanopy_reference_height`: the two methods differed only by the conversion that `atmos_elevation_rel_ground` already does, so they are now one method. The old `ReferenceAboveSurface` docstring also said that `h_atmos` was relative to the apparent sink, a copy-paste error.
- Other docstrings and typos:
  - docstrings of `subcanopy_wind`, `subcanopy_forcing`, `atmos_elevation_rel_ground`, `hydraulic_height`, and the `PlantHydraulicsModel` signature;
  - "paramters" and the TOML "hdyraulic";
  - an accurate description for `canopy_subcanopy_min_reference_height`: the 0.5 m floor binds for canopies shorter than about 0.65 m.
- Removed an unused `FT = eltype(dz)` and a stray `;`.
- NEWS:
  - indented the #1907 entry and listed the API changes and the 0.5 m sub-canopy floor;
  - fixed the earlier entry, in the same unreleased section, that still said the default was 2 m.

## Not changed here, for discussion

- **Zhou LAI model.** The #1907 description says the Zhou model now defaults to spatially varying height, but `ZhouOptimalLAIModel` still defaults to the constant `canopy_height`. Its comment (the CLM height ≈ 0 makes `LAI * height` vanish) describes the problem that the new hydraulic-height floor now handles. Either switch the default or update the description and the comment.
- **CI.** The only Buildkite failure of #1907 (build 11487, "Global Run + P Model CPU MPI") is an out-of-memory kill: 26 GB used against the 24 GB limit with 4 MPI ranks. It happens while Julia compiles the regridding in `EnergyHydrology` (`topmodel_fmax`), before any code that #1907 changes runs; the experiment also passes its own Zhou biomass, so the new canopy defaults are not evaluated. The same step passes with the same limit on other recent PRs, so this is most likely a flaky memory peak. I suggest retrying the step, and raising `slurm_mem` if it fails again.

## Testing

Run locally with Julia 1.12 and the `.buildkite` environment (SurfaceFluxes 1.5.0), formatted with JuliaFormatter 2.10.1:

All of these pass:

- `test/shared_utilities/drivers.jl` and `test/shared_utilities/coupled_fluxes.jl`
- `test/standalone/Soil/climate_drivers.jl`: 92/92 for each float type, with the restored comparisons
- `test/standalone/Bucket/snow_bucket_tests.jl`, `test/standalone/Snow/parameterizations.jl`, and `test/standalone/Snow/snow.jl`
- `test/standalone/Vegetation/test_canopy_helpers.jl` and `test/standalone/Vegetation/canopy_model.jl`
- `test/integrated/soil_canopy_lsm.jl`: the new column test fails without the fix (stored soil `Δz_eff` 7.543 m instead of 7.533 m)
- `test/integrated/full_land.jl`: global `LandModel` tests 333/333, inland-water tests 15/15, including the new soil and snow `Δz_eff` checks
- `Test.detect_ambiguities(ClimaLand; recursive = true)` finds no ambiguities.

CI runs the full suite.

----
- [x] I have read and checked the items on the review checklist.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Review fixes for #1907: sub-canopy reference and ClimaCoupler compatibility

body:
## Purpose

The MON column of the annual leaderboards (`*_sim_annual_time_avg_over_all_years.png`) showed the seasonal cycle of the global mean. Most land is in the northern hemisphere, so that curve mostly reflects the north, and the southern seasonal cycle, half a year out of phase, gets averaged into it.

## Content

- The MON panel now shows the seasonal cycle of each hemisphere's mean in one axis:
  - **Color** shows the data source, as in the LAT and IAV columns: black for OBS, red for SIM.
  - **Line style** shows the hemisphere: solid for NH, dashed for SH.
  - Each line keeps its band showing the spread across years.
- The encoding is explained in the first row's panel title, not in a legend: the two hemispheres peak at opposite times of year, so a legend inside the axis would cover a curve in every corner.
- The hemisphere means use the same cos(lat)-weighted `weighted_average_lonlat` as the global mean. Each hemisphere is masked with NaN instead of windowed by latitude, because `weighted_average_lonlat` warns that the latitudes may be in radians when every latitude is negative. A latitude row centered on the equator counts as northern, so each cell belongs to exactly one hemisphere.
- The IAV column and the partitioning leaderboard are unchanged and stay global.

## Testing

Ran every plot that `make_leaderboard_plots` produces for a global `LandModel` (monthly and seasonal leaderboards for ERA5, ILAMB and FlagshipCarbonMetrics, the RMSE boxplots and the partitioning leaderboard) on the output of a 19-year long run, in a fresh `.buildkite` session. All 26 plots were written with no errors or warnings, and I checked the three `*_sim_annual_time_avg_over_all_years.png` by eye.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Split the leaderboard MON panel by hemisphere
